end.summary:
Ishaan practised adding all four sides of rectangles to find perimeter.
Ishaan used 2 × (length + breadth) for an 8 m by 3 m rectangle and got 22 m.
Ishaan found the perimeter of a 50 m by 30 m rectangle as 160 m and three rounds as 480 m.
Ishaan mixed up the perimeter of a square and another polygon while discussing 56; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishaan practised finding rectangle perimeter by adding two lengths and two breadths, then used the same method for three rounds of a 50 m by 30 m rectangle. Ishaan clearly explained why 8 m and 3 m repeat and checked that 3 × 160 = 480. Ishaan later mixed up the square and polygon perimeter when discussing 56, and this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, practise one rectangle and one square using both the repeated-side addition and the formula, then check whether the units are metres.
